City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
January 16, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:02 p.m. , on January 16, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on January 11, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Absent:
Mayor Ury
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
William P. Curley III, City Attorney
W. Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley
CLOSED SESSION
CS1.
Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employee (Assistant City Manager.) The City’s Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Reardon recessed the meeting to Closed Session. Mayor Ury joined the closed session via conference call at 5:05 p.m. from the Fairmont Hotel in San Jose, California. At the hour of 5:59 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Reardon adjourned the closed session and the conference call with Mayor Ury was disconnected. The City Council reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with four members present; Mayor Ury was absent and did not participate in the open session portion of the meeting.
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council gave direction to staff to move forward with the proposal for the Assistant City Manager contract. The vote was 5-0 with Mayor Ury participating via conference call from the Fairmont Hotel in San Jose, California. Staff will prepare the document, as directed and review the proposed agreement with the candidate for the position of Assistant City Manager. The agreement will brought back to the City Council for discussion and action during an open session meeting in the near future.
PRESENTATIONS
P1.
Recognize Mission Viejo's Community Recycling Program Award Winners
Michelle Clark, Waste Management, presented the award to Emily and Karl Somonian
and members of the United FC White GU15 soccer team.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Peter Hughes, M.V.: stated that he represents a firm that is hoping to purchase a piece of property on Marguerite Parkway near Avery. He requested that the City decline any requests to provide tax relief to potential buyers since there are others offering to pay for the property without tax relief.
Lamar Kelsoe, M.V.: suggested that the City Council Meetings start at 7:00 p.m. instead of 6:00 p.m. to accommodate those who work outside of the City. He also requested that the City remove four eucalyptus trees in his neighborhood at the corner of Via Burgos and Alicia Parkway. Lastly, he suggested that there should be two right turn lanes on Marguerite Parkway and Avery Parkway.
Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: thanked staff and the City Council for the new Farmers Market. She also discussed her attendance at a celebration of the late Martin Luther King, Jr. at Mission Viejo Christian Church and she requested that City Council Meetings are not held on Martin Luther King, Jr. Day in the future.
CONSENT CALENDAR
Item 9 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to approve the Consent Calendar as described below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
Mayor Ury
1.
Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.
2.
City Council Minutes
Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of January 3, 2012, as presented.
3.
Check Register Dated December 16, 2011 in the Amount of $1,097,902.56
Ratified the accompanying check register.
4.
Check Register Dated December 23, 2011 in the Amount of $4,004,356.61
Ratified the accompanying check register.
5.
City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for November 2011
Received and filed.
6.
Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report for November 2011
Received and filed.
7.
Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
November 2011
Received and filed.
8.
Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurerâ??s Monthly Report for November 2011
Received and filed.
10.
American Recovery & Reinvestment Act of 2009 (ARRA) - Energy Efficient Light Fixtures and Bulb Replacement Project (CIP 320)
Authorized the approval of change order #1 in an amount not to exceed $60,000.00 to Republic ITS for energy efficient security lighting replacements at Florence Joyner-Olympiad Park, Montanoso Recreation Center, and Sierra Recreation Center.
11.
2012 CDBG Residential Street Resurfacing (CIP 838)
Approved the bid specifications and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids for the subject project.
12.
Amendment No. 1 to the Memorandum of Understanding for the El Toro Road Traffic Light Synchronization Program
Approved Amendment No. 1 to the Memorandum of Understanding C-0-1692 with the Orange County Transportation Authority for the El Toro Road Traffic Light Synchronization Project.
PUBLIC HEARINGS
OLD BUSINESS
13.
Marguerite Tennis Center Renovation Project (CIP 501)
Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to (1) approve Change Order No.4 to the Construction Contract with Western Alta Construction Company in an amount not to exceed $15,000 and (2) adopt Resolution 12-05 Amending the Fiscal Year 2011-2012 Budget for Costs Related to Capital Improvement Marguerite Tennis Center Project (CIP 501) for $25,006.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
Mayor Ury
NEW BUSINESS
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
9.
Ordinance Regarding Sex Offenders in City Parks and Recreation Facilities
Council Member Schlicht stated this item didn’t get the proper public hearing by virtue of its placement on the Consent Calendar and she asked for a staff report.
City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.
Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt Ordinance 12-292 Adding a New Chapter 11.23 of Title 11 to the Mission Viejo Municipal Code Prohibiting Registered Sex Offenders from Entering City parks and Recreation Facilities.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
Mayor Ury
MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS
14.
Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: expressed concern and stated that OCFA should monitor what happens with the Orange County Employees Retirement System (OCERS) because the OCFA budget is impacted by OCERS.
15.
Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Ury was absent therefore there was no report.
17.
SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report
Council Member Kelley announced that the recent meeting of the SCAG TCC was canceled.
16.
San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon presented the report.
STAFF REPORTS
City Manager’s Report
City Manager Wilberg highlighted the fact that the Council will be adjourning the meeting to Wednesday, January 25, 2012, for the purpose of closing-out the redevelopment agency. There will be three items on the agenda which must be dealt-with before the end of the month as the redevelopment agency will go out of business on February 1, 2012.
Council Member Schlicht requested that the January 25 agenda materials be provided in advance of the meeting.
City Attorney’s Report
City Attorney Curley announced that he will make sure that Special Counsel Celeste Brady is aware that the Council would like the materials for the January 25 meeting as soon as possible. He requested that the Council Members route their questions through him so he can make sure they are answered by the appropriate person prior to the meeting.
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
18.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.
Council Member Kelley
19.
Drafts of CUSD Trustee Area Boundary Maps
Council Member Kelley discussed drafts of proposed CUSD Trustee Area boundary adjustments and the impacts on Mission Viejo CUSD residents.
Lamar Kelsoe, M.V.: asked if it is possible to have one Mission Viejo school district instead of two. He believes that one large school district could save millions of dollars.
Council Member Kelley announced that there are two important events on Thursday, January 19, 2012. The Relay for Life Kick-off will be held at the Norman P. Murray Community Center at 6:00 p.m. and the Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce January Mixer will be held at Farrell’s at the Shops at Mission Viejo from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. Council Member Kelley discussed her attendance, yesterday, at the Mission Viejo Christian Church Martin Luther King, Jr. Day celebration. It was the second year of the event and her second year in attendance. She stated that it was a nice honor and focus on the life of a man who brought great change to our nation at a great personal cost. Council Member Kelley also discussed her visit to the new Mission Viejo Farmers Market which will be held every Friday at the Civic Center from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. She noted that she has received excellent feedback and she knows it will be a very popular event with the residents.
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Leckness reiterated Council Member Kelley’s comments on the new Farmers Market. He stated that there is nothing like the taste of a naval orange that was just picked the day before. He also recounted the story of a valuable product that was inadvertently discarded in a box at his place of business. He called Waste Management to explain the problem and Michelle Clark located the truck so he could meet up with the driver to retrieve the box. Council Member Leckness agreed with his colleagues on the wonderful Martin Luther King, Jr. celebration at Mission Viejo Christian Church and he concluded his comments by sharing video of a recent Lord of the Strings performance by the lead guitarist of Supertramp, the world-renowned Carl Verheyen.
Council Member Schlicht
Council Member Schlicht announced that she is a Charter Member of the new Chamber of Commerce and she is also an Ambassador. She invited the community to attend the next Chamber Mixer on Thursday, January 19, from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. The Chamber has over 100 members and these mixers provide a good opportunity for networking. She stated that she is looking forward to seeing the Chamber’s membership grow. Council Member Schlicht expressed her thanks to Orange County District Attorney Tony Rackauckas for introducing the idea of creating child safety zones and she thanked City Attorney Curley for drafting an ordinance for Mission Viejo. Council Member Schlicht stated that on this day, we honor a monumental historical figure and she ended with a quote from Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr.: “Almost always, the creative dedicated minority has made the world better.”
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that she will not be able to attend the Relay for Life Kick-off event as she will be in Sacramento attending a League of Cities Committee meeting. She outlined her attendance at recent events including an ACCOC meeting last Thursday on the pros and cons and the unintended consequences of cities contracting for services. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon noted that it was great meeting with great representation from throughout the county. She also attended the City’s new Farmers Market and she too heard wonderful things from residents and she is still enjoying the apples that she purchased. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon reiterated the comments on the Martin Luther King, Jr. celebration at Mission Viejo Christian Church. She noted that it was a celebration of diversity and she was impressed to see how far the country has come since Mr. King’s assassination. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon shared a quote from Martin Luther King, Jr. which has impacted her and which was Mr. King’s definition of courage: “"Cowardice asks the question, ’Is it safe?’ Expediency asks the question, ’Is it politic?’ Vanity asks the question, ’Is it popular?’ But, conscience asks the question, ’Is it right?’ And there comes a time when one must take a position that is neither safe, nor politic, nor popular, but one must take it because one’s conscience tells one that it is right."
Mayor Ury
Mayor Ury was absent.
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 7:18 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon adjourned the meeting to Wednesday, January 25, 2012, at 5:00 p.m.
______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
Approved at the meeting of February 06, 2012
